reason: The cited evidence supports that local chemical fluctuation relates to thermal conductivity (E1) and that force-constant fluctuations in HEAs are comparable to binary alloys (E3), but no evidence is provided for the machine learning framework's predictive superiority or its ability to generalize from binary/ternary to HEA systems.
premises: Local chemical disorder in HEAs can be described by mass variance, electronegativity differences, and force-constant fluctuations.
These descriptors correlate with enhanced phonon scattering and reduced lattice thermal conductivity.
Force-constant fluctuations in single-phase HEAs are modest and comparable to those in binary alloys.
A machine learning model trained on binary/ternary data can predict low thermal conductivity in HEAs.
The ML approach will outperform traditional DFT/empirical methods in accuracy and speed.
